items.title: Trump schedules two Texas rallies for Paxton on Oct 27 — Lubbock then Waco; Talarico stages dueling Lubbock rally the same evening
items.summary: The RNC announced Oct 19 that Trump will hold a Lubbock rally (remarks 2:30 p.m.) and a Waco rally (6 p.m.) on Tuesday, Oct 27 — one week before Election Day — for Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton. It is Trump's fourth Texas visit of the cycle (Denton Oct 1, San Antonio Oct 7, Dallas convention). Democrat James Talarico will hold his own rally at Texas Tech's Frazier Alumni Pavilion in Lubbock the same evening (doors 6 p.m.), turning the day into a head-to-head showcase of the tightening Senate race. Recent polls show Talarico leading Paxton narrowly (UH 48-46, Marist 47-45, CBS 51-49, all within MoE).

items.event_time_ist: Oct 20, 2026 (GA Secretary of State announcement; in-person figures as of before noon)
items.title: Georgia crosses 1 million early votes — 12% above the 2022 pace with two weeks to go
items.summary: Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger's office announced Oct 20 that early voting passed 1 million ballots, with 1,007,015 Georgians casting in-person early votes as of before noon Tuesday — a 12% increase over the same point in 2022 and roughly 14.3% of active registered voters. Women make up 54.9% of voters so far; 65-69 year-olds are the largest age bloc (140,000+ ballots). Raffensperger: 'We continue to break records each day of early voting.' The state features the Ossoff-Collins Senate race (Cook: Likely D) and the toss-up Jackson-Bottoms governor's race.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 20, 2026 (MI Secretary of State release; figures as of 7 a.m.)
items.title: Michigan: 789,572 ballots cast two weeks out; mail-ballot requests up 17% vs 2022
items.summary: The Michigan Secretary of State's office reported Oct 20 that 789,572 voters have cast ballots — 789,476 absentee ballots returned plus 96 in-person early votes — representing 10.7% of active registered voters. Voters requested 2,121,458 mail ballots (including 2,001,574 on the permanent mail list), a 17% increase from the same point before the 2022 midterms. Officials urged hand-delivery of absentee ballots rather than mailing. Statewide in-person early voting sites open Saturday, Oct 24 through Sunday, Nov 1.

items.event_time_ist: Poll released Oct 18, 2026 (fielded Oct 9-13; n=2,545 adults)
items.title: Post-ABC News-Ipsos: Trump approval falls to 33%, a record low; Democrats +8 on House ballot; 58-39 want a Democratic check on Trump
items.summary: The Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll (released Oct 18) put Trump's approval at 33% with 66% disapproving — his lowest reading ever in Post-ABC polling, down 4 points since July; 52% strongly disapprove. Democrats lead the generic House ballot by 8 points among registered and likely voters (52-44 among likely voters), up from +3 in July. By 58-39, registered voters prefer a Democratic Congress acting as a check on Trump over a Republican one — a margin that roughly doubled from a year ago. For the first time since 2014, Democrats lead on trust to handle the economy (40-33). Seventy-two percent say the country is on the wrong track; 65% call the Iran military action a mistake; 48% say their finances worsened since Trump returned to office (highest since 1986).

items.event_time_ist: Poll released Oct 18, 2026 (fielded Sept 28-Oct 12; n=19,135 adults; SurveyMonkey-powered)
items.title: NBC News Decision Desk poll: Trump at 34% (second-term low); Democrats +10 (55-45) on congressional control; 71% say wrong track
items.summary: The NBC News Decision Desk national poll (released Oct 18) found Trump's approval at 34% with 66% disapproving — a second-term low, with 51% strongly disapproving (also a term high). Among registered voters, 55% prefer Democrats to control Congress vs 45% for Republicans, and 71% of adults say the country is on the wrong track — the highest wrong-track reading of Trump's second term. The economy is the top issue (31%); only 27% approve of Trump's handling of inflation/cost of living. Just 14% of adults believe they will ever receive Trump's promised $5,000 'dividend' if Republicans win. Both parties are underwater: Democrats 43% favorable/57% unfavorable, Republicans 37%/63%.
